name: Prague Airport

runway.v: two runways; the longest is 06/24, 3,715 m long and 45 m wide (12/30 is 3,250 m × 45 m)

handling.v: business aviation handling by Bell Textron Prague, ABS Jets and Time Air (all-flight handlers: Czech Airlines Handling, Menzies Aviation, Czech GH)
handling.quote: ABS Jets, a.s. − Business Aviation Handling

fuel.v: Jet A-1 and AVGAS 100LL, fuelling H24
fuel.quote: Fuel: Turbo Fuel JET A-1, AVGAS 100 LL

noise.v: the operator states a limited number of coordinated operations in the night period and restricted access for aircraft without ICAO Annex 16 noise certification; details in AIP LKPR AD 2.21
noise.quote: Limited number of coordinated operations in night time period.

slots.v: co-ordinated airport; arrival and departure slots must be requested from the airport co-ordinator before every flight (except emergencies, life-saving and search and rescue)
slots.quote: PRAHA/Ruzyně Airport is a co-ordinated airport.

curfew.v: aircraft over 45 t MTOW that are not on the list of types permitted for night operation may not take off or land 22:00-06:00 local (2100-0500 UTC in winter, 2000-0400 UTC in summer); aircraft of 45 t or less are permitted at night; delayed movements are allowed until 2200 (2100) UTC
curfew.quote: of aircraft types permitted for night operation are not permitted from 2100 (2000) to 0500 (0400).

max_aircraft.v: open to aircraft up to Boeing 747-400 size (wingspan 65 m, length 71 m); larger types such as the A380 only under listed conditions
max_aircraft.quote: LKPR is available for aircraft up to size of Boeing 747-400 (wingspan 65 m, fuselage length 71 m).

notes: The ANS CR HTML page (effective 1 Oct 2026) ends after AD 2.17; AD 2.18–2.24 (local regulations, noise and night rules) are in a separate PDF that could not be opened (permission not given in time). The airport page confirms a night limit but gives no times, so no curfew window is recorded. Bell Textron Prague is listed as 'Executive Aircraft Handling' and Time Air as 'Business Aviation Handling'. Re-researched 2026-10-29: Source is the full AD 2 LKPR text PDF as reissued with AIP AMDT 12/26, effective 29 Oct 2026 (today); AMDT 12/26 changed only refuelling with passengers on board and de-icing; facts already on file should be re-checked against it. Night-rule times: the AIP states times in UTC and AIP GEN 2.1 says 'all hours of operation stated in brackets are applicable during Central European Summer Time', so 2100-0500 UTC (winter) and 2000-0400 UTC (summer) are both 22:00-06:00 local. The night ban applies only to aircraft over 45 t MTOW not on the approved night list (quote for lighter aircraft: 'Take-offs and landings of aircraft with MTOW less or equal to 45 t are permitted from 2100 (2000) to 0500 (0400).'); most business jets are 45 t or less, so the portal's red curfew flag overstates the rule for them. Aircraft certified to ICAO Annex 16 Chapter 2 or uncertified may not take off or land at all. AD 2.20 gives no PPR rule; IATA code not stated in the AIP. Coordinates converted from 50°06'03"N 014°15'36"E.
